overview_pre: This page brings together several **pigmented and epidermal birthmarks**, each in its own short section.
kf: **Congenital dermal melanocytosis** (Mongolian spot): blue-grey patches on the sacrum in darker-skinned babies; **document at birth** (not bruising).
**Naevus of Ota**: blue-grey patch around the eye (V1/V2): check for **glaucoma**; laser is effective.
**Becker naevus**: brown hairy patch on the shoulder appearing in adolescent males.
**Naevus depigmentosus / anaemicus**: stable pale patches; ash-leaf macules may signal **tuberous sclerosis**.
**Linear epidermal naevus**: warty streaks along Blaschko lines; extensive forms may be syndromic.
myths: **"Blue patches on a baby are bruises"**: Mongolian spots are common; record them to avoid safeguarding confusion.
comp: Glaucoma (Ota); tuberous sclerosis associations; psychosocial impact.
prog: Mongolian spots fade over childhood; most others persist.
